name: Şırnak
summary_text: No Şırnak-specific trans statute, enforcement series or incident pattern was found in this pass. The prior estimate flags this province as a far-south-east conflict zone, but the three sources here contain no provincial evidence either way — so the record rests entirely on the country-wide picture: a leaked October 2025 judicial package would criminalise conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' (up to 3 years) and same-sex ceremonies (up to 4 years), raise the minimum age for gender-affirming healthcare to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate, and expose patients (up to 3 years) and providers (up to 7 years) to charges; the 2025 national monitoring report recorded 6 right-to-life violations (3 hate-motivated killings), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (51 in 2024), 313 liberty violations with 299 detention decisions, and 'Year of the Family' directives driving rainbow-symbol bans with expression violations rising from 216 to 540. Where a province is marked by armed conflict and heavy security presence, no-documentation should be read as least-likely-to-document rather than least-likely-to-occur.

sources.title: Türkiye: Draft Law Threatens LGBT People with Prison | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (29 October 2025): the leaked 11th Judicial Package would amend the penal and civil codes to criminalise conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' (up to 3 years) and same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies (up to 4 years); raise the minimum age for gender-affirming healthcare from 18 to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate and government-hospital evaluations; and enable charges against patients (up to 3 years) and providers (up to 7 years); 15 LGBTI+ groups and the national medical association protested; the European Court of Human Rights' Bayev v Russia precedent is cited as making such amendments incompatible with the human-rights convention.

Kaos GL (24 February 2026): presentation of its LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025, titled 'The Year of the Family: A Major Siege' — in 2025 hostility became explicit state policy (presidency-centred directives, the family ministry as implementing body, religious-broadcast censorship, first closure of an LGBTI+ organisation in years); monitoring recorded 6 right-to-life violations (3 hate-motivated killings), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (51 in 2024), 313 liberty violations with 299 detention decisions, private-life violations rising from 16 to 67 (including obstruction of hormone therapy), 61 movement violations (travel bans), expression violations rising from 216 to 540 with rainbow-symbol bans as a major source, 336 assembly violations and 40 association violations.

sources.title: İstanbul police detain trans women for ID checks amid profiling concerns
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (JS-rendered page, only navigation recovered); the source documents a 31 July 2025 mass ID-check roundup in which police detained trans women, recorded their names and videos, and gave no official reason for detention — detainees called it 'profiling'.
